architecture: hybrid, not single hub-lock. One hub-locked circular metro line (Glasgow Subway, hub Buchanan Street, no termini) PLUS two independent National Rail station groups (Glasgow Central, Glasgow Queen Street) that are NOT connected by rail and are NOT merged with each other or with the Subway hub. See jim-handoff.md before wiring an adapter.

ARCHITECTURE: this city has TWO independent networks under one city id, following the established 'do not force a single hub' pattern (same principle as london-se-national-rail's Option A, applied here at a much smaller scale — 2 NR groups, not 7). Glasgow Subway is a genuine hub-lock (Buchanan Street, one circular line). National Rail is NOT hub-locked to Buchanan Street or to each other: Glasgow Central and Glasgow Queen Street are separate buildings, not rail-connected, serving different corridors (Central: cross-border south/England via Avanti + ScotRail through-running; Queen Street: Scottish regional north via ScotRail only). Do not collapse Central and Queen Street into one board, and do not merge either of them into the Subway's Buchanan Street hub.

doNotGroup is required: Buchanan Street (Subway, SPT) vs Glasgow Queen Street (National Rail, GLQ CRS) — connected by a travelator but are separate station entities, separate operators, presumably separate fare/gate systems. The travelator is an interchange path, not a merge. Likewise St Enoch (Subway) vs Glasgow Central (National Rail, GLC CRS) — 'within a short walk' per report, not connected, not a merge.

Neither National Rail group needs INTERNAL doNotGroup the way London Bridge/Liverpool Street did in london-se-national-rail: Glasgow Central has ScotRail + Avanti West Coast, Glasgow Queen Street has ScotRail only, and the report gives no evidence of separate platform/boarding-section logic at either (unlike the London report's explicit per-operator platform language). Treat each as one flat departure board distinguished by destination + operator, same as London Victoria (Southern + Gatwick Express, one board) rather than London Bridge (three boards).

Glasgow Subway is a TRUE CIRCULAR LINE WITH NO TERMINI — a first for this pipeline (Newcastle/Rotterdam/every prior metro had named termini). Direction is signed on the ground as Inner Circle (anticlockwise) and Outer Circle (clockwise), not as 'towards <terminus>'. See direction-model-memo.md — do not invent a terminus-based label for this line.

Subway real-time status: UNKNOWN. No GTFS-RT feed found for SPT (report line 79-83, 111-117). Schedule-only v1, HIGH SKIP RISK flagged by Nico and carried forward here unresolved. Do not assume real-time is available.
